integration_issues.issue: After opening a car (scrollY=2400 -> detail scrollY=0 OK) and clicking data-testid='back-to-results-button', SearchPage lands with window.scrollY=0 instead of restoring ~2400. window.history.state.usr is null on the results page, and injected scrollTo() logging shows only scroll-to-0 calls fire — no scrollTo(0,2400) restore call is ever emitted. Root cause is almost certainly the URL rewriter in /app/frontend/src/pages/SearchPage.js line ~299 (setSearchParams(..., { replace: true }) inside a useEffect) clobbering location.state before the restore effect at line 105-125 can consume it. The module-level `pendingRestore` guard captures at line 103 only if location.state?.restoreScroll is still present at that render. In practice history.state.usr becomes null before restore fires.

action_items: Fix scroll-restore regression in /app/frontend/src/pages/SearchPage.js: ensure the URL-mirror useEffect (setSearchParams(..., { replace: true })) does NOT overwrite navigation state carrying restoreScroll. Options: (a) capture pendingRestore synchronously at module scope on very first import via a useLayoutEffect / render read that always runs before the mirror effect; (b) call setSearchParams with an explicit { replace: true, state: location.state } to preserve state; (c) use useLayoutEffect for the restore before the mirror runs; (d) key the restore effect on location.pathname+location.state so a replaceState that nulls state doesn't cancel it.
Optionally also handle location.key stability: after a replace, key does not change, so the restore effect currently only has one chance to run on mount.

rca of the issue: Back-to-results scroll restore: CarDetailPage.goBack navigates to '/' with { state: { restoreScroll: <scrollY> } }. SearchPage renders, but a useEffect (line 297-300) synchronously mirrors the current query string via setSearchParams(..., { replace: true }). react-router's replaceNavigation drops navigation state (location.state becomes null on the next render, and history.state.usr = null on the DOM), so by the time the restore useEffect (line 105-125) polls pendingRestore, the module-level variable is still null because location.state?.restoreScroll was read only once during render but that render happened AFTER the mirror effect already replaced state (or on a re-render where state is already gone). Injected scrollTo logging confirms only scroll-to-0 calls fire; no scrollTo(0, 2400) is ever attempted. Mitigation: pass state through the setSearchParams call, or persist restoreScroll in sessionStorage keyed by history.state key, or move the restore capture into useLayoutEffect that runs before the mirror effect.
